newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble eases as funds flow in.
newsitem.headline: Rouble eases as funds flow in.

text.p: The rouble eased on Friday as funds flowed into the currency market, especially from the T-bill market where yields are falling.
"The dollar is at the higher limit of the central bank's rates...Some local banks, unhappy about lower yields of T-bills could be buying dollars," European Trade Bank dealer Yevgeny Yakubovsky said.
He said some extra funds could have come back to the market after banks had finished reserving funds and squaring balances in the quarter-end.

Roubles for today settlement were quoted at 5,434-36 per dollar compared with an early 5,430-33 and 5,430-32 late on Thursday. Tomorrow roubles dipped to 5,434.00-5,434.50 per dollar from yesterday's late 5,430-32.
The central bank said it had set 5,424/5,434 as its bid and offer rates against the dollar on Thursday.
Overnight rouble credits yielded 0.5-5.0 percent, the same as late yesterday. They had been relatively steady at around 40-70 percent over the previous two weeks.
"Some banks could be keeping free funds out of this market, which is perhaps why overnight credit rates were higher then, but not too much," Menatep Bank dealer Mikhail Zaretsky said.
